gaps.sentence: We stopped ___ something to eat at the motorway services.
gaps.explanation: 'Stopped to get' = paused for the purpose; 'stopped getting' would mean quit eating.

gaps.sentence: He went on ___ even after the audience had left.
gaps.explanation: go on + -ing = continue the same activity; go on to do = do something next.

gaps.sentence: It's high time we ___ this attic.
gaps.explanation: it's (high) time + subject + past simple (unreal past): time we cleared.

gaps.sentence: Could you help me ___ these boxes upstairs?
gaps.explanation: help takes a bare infinitive or to-infinitive: help me (to) carry. Both accepted.

gaps.sentence: I'm learning ___ the guitar at the moment.
gaps.explanation: learn takes the to-infinitive (learn how to play).

gaps.sentence: When I was a student, I used ___ in shared flats.
gaps.explanation: used TO + infinitive = past habit/state: used to live. (Compare: be used to living.)

gaps.sentence: She suggested ___ the meeting until Monday.
The scheme aims ___ younger visitors to the museum.
gaps.explanation: aim + to-infinitive: aims to attract (aim at + -ing is also possible in BrE).
